title: Securities Trading & Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, Executives, the Company Secretary, and other persons designated as Restricted Persons, including their associated parties (e.g. spouses, dependents, family trusts, and companies).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors and the Managing Director; distinguished for exceptional-circumstances clearance (Chairperson approves) and for ASX notification of trades to the Company Secretary within 2 business days under Listing Rule 3.19A.

tiers.name: other employees and contractors
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are not Directors or the Managing Director; distinguished for exceptional-circumstances clearance (Managing Director or Company Secretary approves).

tiers.name: Associated Party
tiers.description: A person or entity whose trading activity is reasonably within the control or influence of a Restricted Person, including close family members and related entities.

windows.start_anchor: day the Company announces its NTA or estimated NTA to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: same day, unless that NTA announcement falls within five business days before the announcement of a dividend or capital management initiative (in which case the exception does not apply, unless otherwise agreed by the Board)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, in its absolute discretion, may impose a trading embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their associated parties at any time, regardless of whether the trading window is open. Confidentiality is not addressed.

rules.detail: Options and rights over Company securities are expressly named as within the hedging prohibition and require prior Board approval regardless of venue; the policy has no unvested/vested distinction as it does not reference an equity incentive plan.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into any hedging arrangements over the Company's securities (including options or rights) without prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Absolute requirement of prior Board approval before any hedging arrangement over Company securities, with no carve-out and no defined term for 'hedging' itself.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into any hedging arrangements over the Company's securities (including options or rights) without prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Monetisation instruments (e.g. prepaid forwards) are not named; agreeing to dispose of Company securities is a Dealing under 2.8, so monetisation requires trading during an open Trading Window (with prior notification and clearance) or Chairperson clearance in a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: Dealing or Trading: Includes applying for, acquiring, disposing of, or agreeing to apply for, acquire, or dispose of any securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban 'under any circumstances', expressly extended to any derivative or financial instrument used to profit from a share price decline. A purchased put is capable of falling within this wording even though it is a hedge rather than a directional short.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities under any circumstances. Short selling includes any transaction where a person seeks to profit from a decline in the Company's share price, including through derivatives or other financial instruments.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not listed in the Dealing definition.

CFDs are not named; as 'other financial products or financial instruments' referable to HM1 they fall within Securities, so dealing in them is a Dealing requiring Trading Window/clearance, and a short CFD position would also trigger the section 9.3 short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: Securities: Includes shares, debentures, notes, options, other derivatives, interests in managed investment schemes, or other financial products or financial instruments traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Company securities may not be included in a margin lending arrangement without prior approval; the clause is internally inconsistent as to whether the Company or the Board is the approver, but on either reading a secured loan of this kind needs sign-off before it can proceed.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not include the Company's securities in a margin lending arrangement without prior written approval from the Company without prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities outside a 'margin lending arrangement' is not named, and the Dealing definition (applying for, acquiring, disposing of) does not sweep in granting security.
Only margin lending arrangements are named (9.2); there is no broader restriction on other secured financing in respect of Company securities.
No minimum holding period, LIFO rule, or intention-based short-term dealing restriction is stated.

clearance.evidence: Trading Window: A period designated by the Company ... during which Restricted Persons may trade, subject to prior notification and clearance.
Restricted Persons must not enter into any hedging arrangements over the Company's securities (including options or rights) without prior approval of the Board.

In cases of severe financial hardship or other legal/regulatory obligations, the Chairperson may authorise a sale (but not purchase) of shares during a blackout period. Such authorisation must be in writing and specify a time limit.
Requests must be submitted to: ... The Managing Director or Company Secretary (for other employees and contractors).

exceptions.evidence: Participating in or allowing entitlements to lapse under rights issues, DRPs, or equal access buy-backs
Accepting takeover offers or court-approved schemes
Transfers where there is no change in beneficial ownership
Transfers to superannuation or savings schemes
Trades in managed funds where investments are at third-party discretion

exemption_authority: Chairperson may grant written clearance to sell (not purchase) during a Blackout Period for severe financial hardship or overriding legal/regulatory obligations, specifying a time limit (Managing Director or Company Secretary approves for non-Director employees/contractors). No separate exemption exists from the Board-approval requirement for hedging arrangements or margin lending.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short selling includes any transaction where a person seeks to profit from a decline in the Company's share price, including through derivatives or other financial instruments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A purchased put, which profits when the HM1 share price falls, is capable of being characterised as prohibited short selling under this broad wording even though it functions as a hedge, so Board approval should expressly address and carve the put out of the section 9.3 prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not include the Company's securities in a margin lending arrangement without prior written approval from the Company without prior approval of the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The internally inconsistent drafting leaves unclear whether Company approval, Board approval, or both are required for the loan leg of a funded collar, so the safest course is to obtain Board sign-off before the loan is put in place.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy sets out the legal obligations and internal procedures relating to the buying and selling of Hearts and Minds Investments Limited ('the Company') and other securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: HM1 is a listed investment company with no equity incentive plan referenced and no minimum shareholding requirement, so a funded collar over a director's or executive's holding is assessed purely as an ordinary Restricted Person dealing, not against unvested-security rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board retains absolute discretion to impose a trading embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their associated parties at any time, regardless of whether the trading window is open.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, unwind of, or settlement under the collar can be blocked at any time at the Board's unfettered discretion, independent of the scheduled Trading Window/Blackout Period structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any Restricted Person must furnish HM1 with broker statements or activity statements in relation to securities accounts that the Restricted Person has control over if requested to do so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: HM1 can compel disclosure of the bank collar and loan account statements if it suspects a breach, so the arrangement cannot be kept confidential from the Company on request.

summary: A funded collar is conditionally possible for HM1 Restricted Persons, but only with prior Board approval: section 9.1 requires Board approval before any hedging arrangement over Company securities including options or rights, capturing both legs of an OTC collar, and section 9.2 requires approval (worded inconsistently as to whether the Company or the Board is the approver) before Company securities are used in a margin lending arrangement, which would capture the loan secured on the collared shares. Neither approval turns on vesting, since the policy has no unvested-security, equity-plan or minimum shareholding concept. Execution must also sit within the open Trading Window (broadly, the day HM1 announces its NTA) or obtain Chairperson (or Managing Director/Company Secretary for non-Director staff) written clearance to sell during a Blackout Period on hardship or legal-necessity grounds only, and remains subject to the Board's unfettered power to impose a trading embargo at any time. A material risk is that the purchased put, which profits from a share price decline, could be characterised as prohibited 'short selling' under the policy's broad definition, so Board approval should expressly carve the put out of that prohibition. Directors must also notify the Company Secretary of the resulting trades within 2 business days for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A reporting.
